questions.question: Which organization has developed and engineered Induct UV-C disinfectant system for HVAC ducts which has wide applications for disinfecting mechanically ventilated indoor spaces with a view to prevent the spread of Covid-19 like viruses, fungi, mold, bacteria etc?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CSIR-CSIO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CSIR-CSIO (Central Scientific Instruments Organisation)** has developed the Induct UV-C disinfectant system.
 
• This system is designed to disinfect HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) ducts in mechanically ventilated indoor spaces.
 
• The disinfectant system uses **UV-C light technology** to eliminate viruses, bacteria, fungi, and mold, including Covid-19-like pathogens.
 
• The technology is aimed at ensuring safer indoor environments in public and private spaces such as offices, malls, and hospitals during and post-pandemic.
 
• CSIR-CSIO is one of the constituent laboratories of the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)**, which focuses on advanced instrumentation and applied research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UV-C Technology**

 
 
• UV-C light is a type of ultraviolet light with wavelengths between 200-280 nanometers.
 
• It is effective in inactivating microorganisms by breaking their DNA or RNA, preventing replication.
 
• UV-C systems are widely used for sterilization in healthcare, water purification, and air disinfection.
 
 
 
• **CSIR-CSIO**
 
 
• Based in Chandigarh, CSIR-CSIO is a national laboratory under CSIR.
 
• It specializes in the development of scientific instruments and applied research in fields like optics, electronics, and biomedical devices.
 
 
 
• **HVAC Systems**
 
 
• HVAC stands for Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning systems.
 
• These systems regulate indoor temperature, air quality, and humidity levels.
 
• Disinfection of HVAC ducts is crucial in preventing the airborne spread of pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Role of CSIR in Covid-19 Response**
 
 
• CSIR has been at the forefront of India's fight against Covid-19, developing diagnostics, therapeutics, and disinfection solutions.
 
• Its initiatives include genome sequencing, vaccine research, and the development of innovative technologies like the Induct UV-C system.

questions.question: Self-respect movement which was started by EV Ramaswamy Naicker is related to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Self-Respect Movement was initiated by **EV Ramaswamy Naicker, popularly known as Periyar**, in Tamil Nadu in 1925.
 
• The movement aimed to promote rational thinking, self-respect, and equality, especially among the marginalized communities in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It sought to eradicate caste discrimination and challenge the dominance of Brahmanical ideology in Tamil society.
 
• Periyar emphasized the importance of education, gender equality, and social justice as the cornerstone of the movement.
 
• The Self-Respect Movement played a significant role in shaping the socio-political landscape of Tamil Nadu and laid the foundation for Dravidian ideologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **EV Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar)**

 
 
• Periyar was a social reformer, thinker, and politician who advocated for the rights of marginalized communities, particularly Dalits and women.
 
• He strongly opposed the caste system and superstitions prevalent in Indian society.
 
• He is regarded as the "Father of the Dravidian Movement" for his significant contributions to social justice and rationalism.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Movement**
 
 
• The Dravidian Movement emerged from the principles of the Self-Respect Movement and aimed to establish social justice in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It emphasized regional pride, linguistic identity, and opposition to Hindi imposition.
 
• The movement led to the rise of political parties like the DMK (Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam) and AIADMK (All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam).
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Self-Respect Movement**
 
 
• It led to the questioning of traditional social norms and practices, including arranged marriages and religious rituals.
 
• Empowered marginalized communities to demand equality and rights in Tamil society.
 
• Contributed to the spread of progressive ideologies and reforms in Southern India.
 
 
 
• **Key Concepts Promoted by the Movement**
 
 
• Rationalism: Advocated logical reasoning over blind belief and superstition.
 
• Self-respect: Encouraged individuals to reject caste-based discrimination and inequality.
 
• Gender Equality: Focused on women's education and rights to achieve societal progress.

questions.question: The tableau of which of the following states showcased its accomplishments in sports during the Republic Day Parade of 2022?

questions.question: According to Koeppen’s climatic scheme of India, which type of climate is denoted by Aw?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical savanna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Koeppen’s climatic classification, **Aw represents Tropical Savanna climate**, characterized by distinct wet and dry seasons.
 
• This climate is prevalent in regions with **high temperatures throughout the year**, typically above 18°C, and marked by seasonal rainfall patterns.
 
• In India, the Aw climate is observed in areas such as **parts of the Deccan Plateau, Madhya Pradesh, and the northern parts of the Western Ghats**.
 
• Rainfall in these regions is heavily influenced by the **southwest monsoon**, resulting in a wet season during summer and a dry season in winter.
 
• Vegetation in Tropical Savanna climates includes **grasslands with scattered trees**, adapted to withstand periods of drought.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Koeppen’s Climate Classification:**

 
 
• Developed by Wladimir Koeppen, it is one of the most widely used climate classification systems globally.
 
• It categorizes climates based on temperature and precipitation patterns.
 
• The system uses letter codes such as A (Tropical), B (Dry), C (Temperate), D (Cold), and E (Polar).
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Aw Climate:**
 
 
• Aw stands for Tropical Savanna Climate with winter dryness.
 
• Rainfall occurs predominantly during the summer monsoon season.
 
• Annual precipitation typically ranges between 750 mm to 1250 mm.
 
 
 
• **Vegetation in Aw Climate:**
 
 
• Tropical savanna vegetation consists of grasses and sparse trees such as acacia and baobab.
 
• Plants are adapted to survive long dry periods and occasional wildfires.
 
 
 
• **Indian Climatic Zones:**
 
 
• India’s climate is diverse, ranging from Tropical (A) to Alpine (E).
 
• Koeppen’s classification helps in understanding regional climatic patterns and their impact on agriculture and biodiversity.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: In which of the following years was the Brahmo Samaj established by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1828**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828** in Kolkata, India.
 
• It aimed to reform Hindu society by discarding practices like **Sati, idolatry, and caste discrimination**.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was influenced by monotheistic principles and drew inspiration from the Upanishads.
 
• The organization advocated for **education, women's rights, and the abolition of social evils**.
 
• It played a critical role in the **Bengal Renaissance** and India's broader socio-religious reform movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy:**

 
 
• He is regarded as the "Father of Modern India" for his pioneering role in social and religious reform.
 
• He campaigned against the practice of **Sati** and was instrumental in its abolition in 1829.
 
• He strongly advocated for the **freedom of press** and modern education in India.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of Brahmo Samaj:**
 
 
• To promote monotheism and reject idol worship.
 
• To advocate for **universal brotherhood** and equality among all human beings.
 
• To encourage rational thinking and oppose superstitions.
 
 
 
• **Key Contributions of Brahmo Samaj:**
 
 
• It focused on **abolishing caste discrimination** and untouchability in Indian society.
 
• The organization supported **women’s education** and opposed child marriage and polygamy.
 
• It contributed to the establishment of educational institutions, including the **Hindu College (now Presidency University)** in Kolkata.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj inspired various reform movements across India, including the **Prarthana Samaj** and the **Arya Samaj**.
 
• Its emphasis on rationalism and social justice continues to influence modern Indian thought and governance.

questions.question: Which of the following Sun temples is built by Raja Bhimdev I of the Solanki dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Modhera Sun Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Modhera Sun Temple was built by **Raja Bhimdev I** of the Solanki dynasty in the early 11th century (circa 1026 CE).
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Surya, the Sun God**, and is located in the village of Modhera, Gujarat, India.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **intricate carvings**, architectural precision, and unique alignment with the equinox, allowing sunlight to illuminate the sanctum sanctorum.
 
• The Modhera Sun Temple is considered a prime example of the **Maru-Gurjara architectural style**.
 
• Though no worship is conducted there today, the temple is a protected monument under the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sun Temples in India**

 
 
• Other famous Sun Temples in India include the **Konark Sun Temple** in Odisha and the **Martand Sun Temple** in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• These temples are dedicated to Surya, symbolizing energy, vitality, and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Style**
 
 
• The Maru-Gurjara style, prominent in western India, emphasizes ornate carvings, stepped tanks, and open-air courtyards.
 
• The Modhera Sun Temple exemplifies this style with its **assembly hall (Sabha Mandap), sanctum (Garbhagriha), and stepped reservoir (Kunda)**.
 
 
 
• **Alignment with the Sun**
 
 
• The temple's sanctum is designed in such a way that during the equinox, the first rays of the sun illuminate the idol of Surya.
 
• This alignment reflects the advanced astronomical knowledge of the era.
 
 
 
• **Solanki Dynasty**
 
 
• The Solanki dynasty, also known as the Chaulukya dynasty, ruled parts of present-day Gujarat and Rajasthan between the 10th and 13th centuries.
 
• They were great patrons of art and architecture, as evidenced by monuments like the Modhera Sun Temple and the Rani ki Vav stepwell.

questions.question: As of September 2022, which of the following states has more than 1 Rajya Sabha seat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uttarakhand has a total of **3 Rajya Sabha seats**, as of September 2022.
 
• The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the upper house of the Indian Parliament, and the allocation of seats is based on the population of the state.
 
• Smaller states like Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram have **1 Rajya Sabha seat each** due to their lower population compared to Uttarakhand.
 
• Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies using the system of proportional representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha Overview:**

 
 
• The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of **250 members**, out of which **238 are representatives of states and union territories**, and **12 are nominated by the President of India**.
 
• Members of Rajya Sabha serve a term of **6 years**, with one-third of the members retiring every two years.
 
 
 
• **Seat Allocation in Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• Seats are allocated based on the population of each state as per the latest Census.
 
• States with higher populations (e.g., Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra) have more seats compared to smaller states.
 
 
 
• **Election Process:**
 
 
• Rajya Sabha members are elected by the **MLAs of the respective state legislatures** through proportional representation.
 
• The voting method used is the **Single Transferable Vote (STV)**.
 
 
 
• **Special Features of Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• It is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved like the Lok Sabha.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **legislative review and representation of states** at the national level.

questions.question: When did Government of India launch National Youth Policy (NYP) to cater the needs of youth in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India launched the **National Youth Policy (NYP) 2014** on **February 21, 2014**, to empower and facilitate the development of youth in the country.
 
• The policy focuses on **five priority areas**: education, employment and skill development, entrepreneurship, health and healthy lifestyle, and social values and community engagement.
 
• The NYP 2014 replaces the earlier National Youth Policy of 2003, addressing the current challenges and aspirations of youth aged **15–29 years**.
 
• The policy aims to enable youth to achieve their full potential and contribute to India's development through targeted and inclusive measures.
 
• The NYP 2014 emphasizes promoting **equity and inclusion** to ensure that marginalized and disadvantaged youth have access to resources and opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Youth in NYP 2014:**

 
 
• The policy defines youth as individuals in the age group of **15–29 years**, accounting for approximately **27.5% of India's population** as per Census 2011.
 
• This age group is considered the most productive and dynamic segment of society.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of NYP 2014:**
 
 
• To develop a **productive workforce** capable of contributing to India's economic development.
 
• To instill a **strong sense of community service** and promote active citizenship among youth.
 
• To ensure **equal opportunities** for all youth, particularly those from marginalized sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Programmes under NYP 2014:**
 
 
• The policy facilitates youth development through various schemes like **Skill India, National Service Scheme (NSS), and Start-up India**.
 
• It also integrates existing schemes like the **Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development (RGNIYD)**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India has one of the world's largest youth populations, termed the **‘demographic dividend’**, which provides a unique opportunity for economic growth.
 
• The NYP 2014 aligns with international frameworks like the United Nations **World Programme of Action for Youth**.

questions.question: Which of the state is associated with the Kudumbashree,the largest women empowering project in the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kudumbashree is a **women-centric poverty eradication and empowerment program** launched by the Government of Kerala in 1998.
 
• The initiative operates through a three-tier structure of Community Development Societies (CDS), Area Development Societies (ADS), and Neighbourhood Groups (NHG).
 
• Kudumbashree focuses on **microfinance, entrepreneurship, and women empowerment**, enabling women to engage in economic activities.
 
• It is regarded as the **largest women's empowerment project in India** and has been instrumental in transforming the socio-economic status of women in Kerala.
 
• Kudumbashree's success has inspired similar initiatives across various states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neighbourhood Groups (NHGs):**

 
 
• NHGs are the smallest units of the Kudumbashree initiative, consisting of 10-20 women from economically weaker sections.
 
• These groups provide a platform for women to collaborate and access microfinance services.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance in Kudumbashree:**
 
 
• Kudumbashree provides microfinance services to women, enabling them to start small-scale businesses and improve their financial stability.
 
• It also supports self-help groups in availing loans and financial literacy programs.
 
 
 
• **Entrepreneurship Development:**
 
 
• Kudumbashree promotes entrepreneurship among women through skill development, market linkages, and financial support.
 
• Initiatives include agriculture, handicrafts, food production, and other small-scale industries.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Kudumbashree:**
 
 
• Kudumbashree has empowered over 4.3 million women in Kerala, contributing significantly to poverty alleviation and gender equality.
 
• It has also enhanced community participation and improved the overall socio-economic conditions in the state.

questions.question: The Power of Judicial Review was taken from the Constitution of which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of **Judicial Review** was established in the United States of America through the landmark case of **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**.
 
• Judicial review allows courts to **invalidate laws and executive actions** that are deemed unconstitutional.
 
• The U.S. Constitution provides the framework for judicial review, ensuring the principle of **checks and balances** among the legislative, executive, and judicial branches.
 
• This principle has been widely adopted by other democracies, including India, in their constitutional frameworks.
 
• The Indian Constitution incorporated the power of judicial review under **Articles 13, 32, 226, and 136**, inspired by the U.S. model.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review:**

 
 
• It is the power of the judiciary to ensure that laws passed by the legislature and actions taken by the executive are within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• Judicial review helps maintain the supremacy of the Constitution and prevents arbitrary or unconstitutional actions.
 
• It is considered a cornerstone of constitutional governance in democratic systems.
 
 
 
• **Marbury v. Madison (1803):**
 
 
• It was a landmark case in U.S. legal history where the Supreme Court established its authority to review and strike down unconstitutional laws.
 
• This case was presided over by Chief Justice John Marshall, who laid the foundation for the doctrine of judicial review.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review in India:**
 
 
• India adopted judicial review as a fundamental feature of its Constitution, inspired by the American model.
 
• It is exercised by the Supreme Court and High Courts to ensure that legislative and executive actions comply with constitutional provisions.
 
• Key articles enabling judicial review in India include Article 13 (laws inconsistent with fundamental rights) and Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies).
 
 
 
• **Global Adoption:**
 
 
• Many countries, including South Africa, Canada, and Australia, have adopted judicial review, tailoring it to their specific constitutional frameworks.
 
• It serves as a mechanism for upholding democratic values, protecting individual rights, and ensuring accountability in governance.

questions.question: Which of the following developed a small electric vehicle in 2021 that can change its width on the go?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**City Transformer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **City Transformer** is an Israeli startup that developed a revolutionary small electric vehicle (EV) in 2021.
 
• This EV features a unique ability to **adjust its width on the go**, making it highly adaptable for urban environments.
 
• The vehicle's width can shrink from **1.4 meters to 1 meter** to navigate through congested streets and fit into tight parking spaces.
 
• It is classified as a quadricycle and offers a top speed of **90 km/h**, making it suitable for city commutes.
 
• The vehicle is powered by electric motors and offers a range of up to **180 km** on a single charge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quadricycle Classification:**

 
 
• A quadricycle is a small vehicle that is lighter and less powerful than standard cars, often used for urban mobility.
 
• In the EU, quadricycles are divided into categories like L6e (light quadricycles) and L7e (heavy quadricycles).
 
 
 
• **Urban Mobility Challenges:**
 
 
• Increasing traffic congestion and limited parking spaces are major challenges in modern cities.
 
• Innovative vehicles like City Transformer address these issues by offering compact and flexible designs.
 
 
 
• **Electric Vehicle Advantages:**
 
 
• EVs contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.
 
• They are more energy-efficient compared to internal combustion engine vehicles.
 
 
 
• **City Transformer's Vision:**
 
 
• The company aims to revolutionize urban transportation by providing sustainable and space-efficient mobility solutions.
 
• Its foldable width design is a key innovation for addressing urban infrastructure constraints.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair among the following related to temple architecture.

options.text: Mandapa : Place in temple where people could assemble
Gopuram : Place where the image of the deity is installed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandapa : Place in temple where people could assemble**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mandapa** is an integral part of Indian temple architecture and serves as a pavilion or hall where devotees can gather and assemble for prayers, rituals, and other ceremonies.
 
• It is often located in front of the **Garbhagriha** (sanctum sanctorum) and acts as a transition space for devotees before they reach the deity's chamber.
 
• The design of Mandapas varies across different regions and styles of temple architecture, such as **Nagara, Dravidian, and Vesara**, but they commonly feature carved pillars and ornate ceilings.
 
• Mandapas can be divided into different types such as **Artha-Mandapa** (entrance porch), **Maha-Mandapa** (large hall), and **Kalyana-Mandapa** (used for rituals like weddings).
 
• The Mandapa serves both functional and aesthetic purposes, providing space for communal worship while showcasing intricate carvings and artistic excellence in temple design.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garbhagriha:**

 
 
• The sanctum sanctorum of the temple where the main deity is enshrined.
 
• It is typically a small, dark chamber symbolizing the womb of creation.
 
• Access to the Garbhagriha is usually restricted to priests, who perform rituals and offerings.
 
 
 
• **Shikhara:**
 
 
• The towering superstructure above the Garbhagriha, representing Mount Meru, the mythological axis of the universe.
 
• Shikhara is a hallmark of Nagara-style temples in North India.
 
• In Dravidian temples, the corresponding structure is known as the **Vimana**.
 
 
 
• **Gopuram:**
 
 
• Large, ornate gateways that serve as entrances to South Indian temples, especially in the Dravidian style.
 
• Gopurams are known for their towering height and elaborate carvings depicting deities, mythological stories, and other motifs.
 
• They are symbolic of the threshold between the secular and sacred spaces.
 
 
 
• **Temple Architecture Styles:**
 
 
• **Nagara Style:** Predominantly found in North India, characterized by curvilinear Shikharas.
 
• **Dravidian Style:** Found in South India, known for its pyramidal Vimanas and large Gopurams.
 
• **Vesara Style:** A blend of Nagara and Dravidian styles, mainly seen in Deccan temples.

questions.question: Who succeeded Alivardi Khan as Nawab of Bengal in 1756?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siraj-ud-daula**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Siraj-ud-daula** succeeded Alivardi Khan as the Nawab of Bengal in **1756**.
 
• He was the last independent Nawab of Bengal before the British East India Company established control over Bengal.
 
• Siraj-ud-daula’s reign ended following his defeat in the **Battle of Plassey (1757)**, which marked the beginning of British dominance in India.
 
• He was known for his opposition to the growing influence of the British East India Company in Bengal.
 
• His conflict with the British was a key factor in the political and economic shift in India during the mid-18th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alivardi Khan**

 
 
• Alivardi Khan ruled Bengal from 1740 to 1756 and was known for his administrative skills and military prowess.
 
• He successfully defended Bengal from repeated invasions by the Marathas during his reign.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Plassey (1757)**
 
 
• The battle was fought between the forces of Siraj-ud-daula and the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive.
 
• The British victory in the battle was aided by the betrayal of Siraj-ud-daula by his commander, Mir Jafar.
 
• The battle marked the beginning of British political dominance in India.
 
 
 
• **Mir Jafar**
 
 
• Mir Jafar was installed as the puppet Nawab of Bengal by the British after the Battle of Plassey.
 
• He played a crucial role in the British victory by betraying Siraj-ud-daula.
 
 
 
• **British East India Company’s Expansion**
 
 
• The company utilized political alliances, military power, and economic exploitation to establish control over India.
 
• The Battle of Plassey and subsequent events laid the foundation for the British colonial rule in India.

questions.question: Which of the following policies has revenue and expenditure aspects?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fiscal Policy** involves the government's decisions regarding taxation (revenue) and spending (expenditure) to influence economic activity.
 
• It is primarily used to achieve macroeconomic objectives such as **economic growth, employment generation, and inflation control.**
 
• Fiscal policy can be categorized into two types: **expansionary** (increasing spending or reducing taxes) and **contractionary** (reducing spending or increasing taxes).
 
• It is implemented through the government's budget and requires approval from legislative bodies like the Parliament.
 
• Unlike monetary policy (which is managed by the central bank), fiscal policy is directly controlled by the government. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key components of Fiscal Policy:**

 
 
• **Taxation:** The government collects revenue through various taxes such as income tax, corporate tax, GST, etc.
 
• **Government Spending:** Expenditures include investments in infrastructure, welfare programs, education, healthcare, and defense.
 
• ** Fiscal policy decisions often result in budget deficits (spending exceeds revenue) or surpluses (revenue exceeds spending).
 
 
 
• Balanced Budget:**
 
 
• A balanced budget refers to a situation where **government revenue equals its expenditure**.
 
• While desirable, balanced budgets are often avoided during economic downturns to stimulate growth.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Multiplier:**
 
 
• The fiscal multiplier measures the impact of government spending or taxation changes on overall economic output.
 
• A higher multiplier means fiscal policy is more effective in stimulating the economy.
 
 
 
• **Coordination with Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• Fiscal policy works in tandem with monetary policy (controlled by the central bank) to address economic challenges.
 
• For instance, fiscal stimulus coupled with accommodative monetary policy can boost demand in the economy.

questions.question: According to the census of 2011, which state of India ranks first in terms of population percentage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of 2011, **Uttar Pradesh** ranks first among Indian states in terms of population percentage, contributing approximately **16.5%** to the total population of India.
 
• The state had a population of over **199 million** in 2011, making it the most populous state in India.
 
• Uttar Pradesh accounts for a significant portion of India's population due to factors like high birth rates and large land area.
 
• The state is home to several major cities, including **Lucknow**, **Kanpur**, **Varanasi**, and **Agra**, which contribute to its dense population.
 
• Uttar Pradesh's population growth presents both opportunities and challenges in terms of governance, resource allocation, and infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:**

 
 
• Uttar Pradesh has a population density of approximately **828 people per square kilometer**, as per the 2011 Census.
 
• It is one of the most densely populated states in India.
 
 
 
• **India's Overall Population:**
 
 
• India's total population according to the 2011 Census was approximately **1.21 billion**.
 
• Uttar Pradesh alone accounts for a significant share of the country's total population.
 
 
 
• **Other High Population States:**
 
 
• After Uttar Pradesh, **Maharashtra**, **Bihar**, and **West Bengal** are among the states with high population numbers.
 
• These states also have significant socio-economic influence in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Population Growth:**
 
 
• Rapid population growth in states like Uttar Pradesh poses challenges related to **healthcare, education, employment, and housing**.
 
• It also leads to increased pressure on natural resources and infrastructure.

questions.question: Kuchipudi dance form is named after a village, which exists in which of the following district of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India and is named after the village **Kuchipudi** in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in religious themes and was originally performed as a form of storytelling through dance-drama by male Brahmin priests.
 
• Kuchipudi combines **fast rhythmic footwork**, expressive eye movements, and symbolic hand gestures to narrate stories, often derived from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• The dance is characterized by its graceful movements, intricate costumes, and the use of Carnatic music.
 
• It was revived and popularized in the modern era by renowned practitioners like Siddhendra Yogi and later by artists like Vempati Chinna Satyam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India**

 
 
• India recognizes eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Odissi, Sattriya, and Mohiniyattam.
 
• Each form is distinct in style, costumes, and regional influence but follows the Natya Shastra, the ancient treatise on performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Natya Shastra**
 
 
• A foundational text on Indian classical dance, drama, and music, written by the sage Bharata.
 
• It outlines the principles of **Rasa (emotions), Bhava (expressions), and Mudras (gestures)** in performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Krishna District of Andhra Pradesh**
 
 
• Located in Coastal Andhra, Krishna district is named after the Krishna River, which flows through it.
 
• The district is a cultural hub, home to several temples, historic landmarks, and traditional art forms like Kuchipudi.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music**
 
 
• The classical music tradition of South India, often used as the musical accompaniment in Kuchipudi performances.
 
• It emphasizes intricate melodic patterns (ragas) and rhythmic cycles (talas).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered an industrial concession?

options.text: Subsidy to purchase goods and services

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subsidy to purchase goods and services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Industrial concessions are typically measures provided by governments to promote industrial growth and attract investments.
 
• **Tax concessions** refer to reductions in taxes or exemptions provided to industries to reduce their financial burden and encourage development.
 
• **Tax holidays** are periods during which businesses are exempt from paying certain taxes, often to promote investments in specific sectors or regions.
 
• **Subsidised power supply** involves providing electricity to industries at reduced rates to lower production costs and boost competitiveness.
 
• Unlike the above, **subsidy to purchase goods and services** is generally not categorized as an industrial concession, as it is more aligned with consumer-oriented or welfare policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Concessions:**

 
 
• These are measures like tax breaks, subsidies, and infrastructure support provided to industries to enhance their growth and competitiveness.
 
• They are often part of government policies aimed at regional development, employment generation, and foreign direct investment.
 
 
 
• **Tax Holiday:**
 
 
• A temporary period during which a company or sector is exempt from certain tax obligations.
 
• It is commonly offered to startups or industries in special economic zones (SEZs).
 
 
 
• **Subsidised Power Supply:**
 
 
• Governments often provide electricity at reduced rates to industries to lower production costs.
 
• This concession helps industries become more competitive in domestic and global markets.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies in General:**
 
 
• Subsidies are financial aid provided by governments to reduce the cost of goods and services for consumers or producers.
 
• They can be in the form of direct payments, tax reductions, or reduced prices for resources.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to head a democratic government in Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Benazir Bhutto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Benazir Bhutto was the first woman to lead a democratic government in Pakistan and the Islamic world as Prime Minister.
 
• She served as Prime Minister of Pakistan twice: first from 1988 to 1990 and then from 1993 to 1996.
 
• Her election marked a significant milestone for women's political empowerment in Muslim-majority countries.
 
• Benazir Bhutto was the daughter of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Pakistan's former Prime Minister and President.
 
• She was the leader of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP), which she inherited after her father's execution in 1979.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background on Benazir Bhutto:**

 
 
• Born on June 21, 1953, in Karachi, Pakistan, she was educated at Harvard University and the University of Oxford.
 
• She was the first woman to preside over the Oxford Union debating society.
 
• Her political career was shaped by her father's leadership and tragic execution under a military regime.
 
 
 
• **Significance of her leadership:**
 
 
• Benazir Bhutto's election as Prime Minister symbolized progress in women's participation in politics in a patriarchal society.
 
• She focused on policies related to healthcare, education, and women's rights during her tenure.
 
 
 
• **Challenges during her tenure:**
 
 
• Her administration faced allegations of corruption and struggles with political instability.
 
• She was dismissed from office twice by the President of Pakistan due to various controversies.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Benazir Bhutto was assassinated on December 27, 2007, during a political rally in Rawalpindi.
 
• She remains a symbol of resilience and a trailblazer for women in politics in the Islamic world.

questions.question: Which Bill does the Major Ports Authorities Bill, 2020 repeal with an aim to provide greater autonomy and flexibility to the major ports and to professionalise their governance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Major Port Trusts Act, 1963**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Major Ports Authorities Bill, 2020 seeks to **repeal the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963** to modernize port governance and provide greater autonomy.
 
• The Bill aims to **professionalize the management of major ports** and empower port authorities to make independent financial and operational decisions.
 
• It introduces a Board of Port Authority for each major port, replacing the earlier Port Trust structure.
 
• The Bill emphasizes **improved transparency and efficiency** in port operations by reducing bureaucratic control.
 
• The legislation is designed to **align major ports with international best practices** to enhance competitiveness and attract private investment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Ports in India:**

 
 
• India has 13 major ports, including Mumbai, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, and Cochin.
 
• These ports handle approximately 60% of India’s total cargo traffic.
 
 
 
• **Port Trust System:**
 
 
• Under the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963, major ports were governed by Port Trust Boards.
 
• These boards consisted of government-appointed members, limiting operational flexibility.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Major Ports Authorities Bill, 2020:**
 
 
• Empowers ports to fix tariffs for services and assets without regulatory intervention.
 
• Board members include representatives from state governments, port users, and independent experts.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison:**
 
 
• International ports like Singapore and Rotterdam operate under autonomous management systems.
 
• The Bill aims to bring Indian ports closer to these global standards.
 
 
 
• **Private Investment:**
 
 
• The Bill promotes Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) to drive port development.
 
• Private players are encouraged to participate in cargo handling and port infrastructure projects.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hyderabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)** is a premier institution under the Department of Space, Government of India.
 
• The headquarters of NRSC is situated in **Hyderabad, Telangana**, specifically at Balanagar.
 
• NRSC is responsible for acquiring, processing, and distributing remote sensing data from Indian and foreign satellites.
 
• It plays a critical role in **space-based earth observation** and provides data solutions for various national developmental programs.
 
• NRSC operates several ground stations across India and collaborates with various organizations for satellite data utilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Remote Sensing:**

 
 
• Remote sensing refers to the process of acquiring information about Earth's surface without being in direct contact, using satellites or aircraft.
 
• It involves capturing electromagnetic radiation reflected or emitted by objects and analyzing this data to draw insights.
 
• Applications include agriculture, forestry, water resources, urban planning, disaster management, and environmental monitoring.
 
 
 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):**
 
 
• ISRO is India's national space agency, headquartered in Bengaluru, responsible for space research, satellite launches, and technology development.
 
• NRSC functions as one of ISRO's centers focusing on remote sensing and GIS (Geographic Information Systems) applications.
 
 
 
• **Earth Observation Satellites:**
 
 
• India operates a series of earth observation satellites like Cartosat, Resourcesat, and RISAT for mapping and monitoring purposes.
 
• These satellites provide high-resolution imagery for various applications, including disaster response and climate studies.
 
 
 
• **GIS and Remote Sensing Applications:**
 
 
• Geographic Information Systems (GIS) integrate satellite data with location-based information to provide actionable insights.
 
• NRSC uses GIS technology for projects like crop monitoring, flood mapping, and urban planning.
